title: Temporal surge arbiter with weighted fairness and rollback path
author: Evan Park
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent SLO violations during short-lived multi-region traffic spikes where existing load-shedding and circuit-breaker heuristics either over-ejected tenants or caused thrashing when capacity returned. This PR introduces a TemporalSurgeArbiter: a conservative, time-aware request prioritizer that smooths transient spikes using weighted fairness and exposes a safe rollback path when sustained SLO pressure is detected.

What this changes (single-string summary): Adds a new runtime component (TemporalSurgeArbiter) that sits between the router and node scheduler. It maintains per-tenant ephemeral tokens (surge credits) that decay over a configurable window, applies a weighted-fairness algorithm that combines tenant priority and recent acceptance rate, and attaches a graceful rollback hook that triggers progressive relaxations to avoid mass evictions. The arbiter integrates with the existing SLO enforcer and circuit manager so it can shift from conservative throttling to soft-relaxation (grace window) when health probes indicate recovery.

Key features: 1) Weighted fairness by tenant token budgets and recent latency/errored-token feedback. 2) Temporal decay of surge credits (configurable half-life) to prevent long-term state accumulation after spikes. 3) Soft-rollback path: when SLO violations persist beyond a configured window, the arbiter progressively relaxes thresholds and signals the circuit manager to increase retry headroom instead of immediately widening routes. 4) Backpressure-safe: the arbiter returns clear Retry-After semantics and integrates with client hedging policies. 5) Config-gated rollout behind feature flag surge_arbiter_v1 and runtime config in /etc/redwood/arbiter.yaml.

Compatibility and migration: Backwards compatible by default; the arbiter is disabled unless the feature flag is enabled. Migration steps in the console: enable feature flag for a pilot tenant, monitor slo:request_p99_latency and slo:served_ratio, then enable at region-level. If rollback is needed, disable the feature flag to revert to previous behavior.

Implementation notes: TemporalSurgeArbiter is implemented as a lightweight in-memory controller in serving/runtime/arbiter. It uses a fixed-size LRU for tenant entries to bound memory and a lock-free sampling queue for fairness scoring to minimize added latency. We added telemetry (metrics: arbiter.accepted, arbiter.rejected, arbiter.rollback_steps, arbiter.token_decay_rate) and traces in the request path (span:arbiter.evaluate). The arbiter exposes a gRPC health endpoint for cross-region probes.

Performance results (benchmark-lab): On synthetic spikes (2x baseline QPS for 45s) in the lab we saw p99 latency improvements of ~18% for high-priority tenants and net reduction in eviction events by ~42% versus current soft-evict policy. Cost overhead measured at ~0.9% CPU on serving nodes and sub-0.5ms median added latency in critical path.

Hotfix included: race condition fix in circuit-manager state transitions (fixes a double-commit on fast-reconnect) and a metrics naming bug that hid rollback step counts in older dashboards.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for scoring and decay (serving/runtime/arbiter/*_test.go). Integration tests: staged canary in perf-canary with 3 regions, automated chaos run (simulated node drains) passed. Manual runbook validated rollback path and failure mode (see testing/arbiter-canary-runbook.md).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-482 linked)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Telemetry added and dashboards draft updated
- [x] Feature flag gating and runtime config present
- [x] Compatibility/migration notes written
- [x] Hotfix race condition verified

Rollout plan: 1) Enable for 5 pilot tenants in us-west with observability alerting on slo:served_ratio drop >1% over baseline. 2) Monitor 48 hours, adjust token half-life. 3) Gradual region-by-region enablement with automatic rollback on persistent SLO degradation.

review_comments: Asha Raman: Overall this is promising. Two requests: can we make the token decay half-life configurable per-tenant (or at least per-tenant-class)? Also add a short note about memory bounds for the LRU in the design doc.
Evan Park (author): Good point — added tenant-tier multiplier and documented LRU sizing. Implemented limit to 10k tenant entries by default and added config entry for override.
Luca Meyer: The scoring math looks fine but please add a small comment explaining the tie-breaker (use timestamp) so future maintainers understand determinism.
Evan Park: Added comments and unit tests asserting deterministic ordering for equal scores.
Priya Kapoor: CI flaked on the first run due to test timeout in the perf harness; re-ran and all checks passed. Approving pending minor doc tweak on rollout steps.
Evan Park: Updated the rollout in docs to include explicit Saga-style rollback triggers and monitoring thresholds.
release_notes: Introduces TemporalSurgeArbiter: a time-aware request prioritizer for smoothing transient traffic spikes; includes a conservative rollback path and a race fix in circuit-manager. Feature gated behind surge_arbiter_v1.
notes_for_oncall: If enabled and you see sustained decrease in served_ratio >2% for >30m, flip surge_arbiter_v1 off to revert immediately. Monitor arbiter.rollback_steps and arbiter.rejected metrics to assess impact.
